\begin{definition}[Register configurations]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Regs}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Regs}
\leanok
A register configuration is a collection of 21 natural-number registers, named $L$, $P$,
$A$, $B$, $S$, $N_1$, $W_p$, $E$, $F$, $E_2$, $F_2$, $\text{Pos}$, $\text{Pos}_2$, $T$,
$U$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, $Q_4$, $\text{Cap}$, and $Z$; each register has default value
$0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register-value function]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Regs.val}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Regs.val}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Regs}
For a register record $R$, define its value function on the indices $0,\ldots,20$ by
assigning the values of $L$, $P$, $A$, $B$, $S$, $N_1$, $W_p$, $E$, $F$, $E_2$, $F_2$,
$\text{Pos}$, $\text{Pos}_2$, $T$, $U$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, $Q_4$, $\text{Cap}$, and $Z$
to indices $0$ through $20$, respectively.
\end{definition}

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Updating the third query register]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_Q3}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_Q3}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.rQ3}
\difficulty{4}
Let $R$ be a record of natural-number registers, and let $v\in\mathbb N$. Replacing the
entry at coordinate $17$ in its length-$21$ vector of register values by $v$ gives the
vector of register values of the record obtained by setting its third query register to
$v$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $R$ be a record of natural-number registers, and let $v\in\mathbb N$. Replacing the

$v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Updating the Cap register]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_Cap}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Regs.upd_Cap}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.rCap}
\difficulty{4}
For any register record $R$ and natural number $v$, updating the indexed register
corresponding to $Cap$ in the register-value function of $R$ to $v$ gives the
register-value function of the record obtained by replacing $R.Cap$ with $v$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $R$ be a record of natural-number registers, and let $v\in\mathbb N$. Replacing the
entry at coordinate $20$ in its length-$21$ vector of register values by $v$ gives the

\begin{definition}[Bounded register record]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Regs}
A register record $R$ is bounded by a natural number $B$ when every one of its 21
register values is at most $B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Register values inherit the bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd.val_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val}
\difficulty{4}
If every named register of a register record $R$ is at most $B$, then the value of every
one of its 21 indexed registers is at most $B$.
\end{lemma}
